title: Yindan Xinnaotong Soft Capsule improves post-ischemic stroke recovery by regulating CREB/BDNF-mediated synaptic plasticity and CREB/VEGFA-mediated angiogenesis.
authors: Cheng, Cuicui; Liu, Huijuan; Guan, Guoqiang; Fei, Qinglin; Zhao, Mengtao; Wang, Huanyi; Wang, Ruirui; Hu, Limin; Li, Xing; Wu, Honghua; Fan, Guanwei; Jiang, Miaomiao; Zhu, Yan; Lyu, Ming
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药YD通过CREB/BDNF和CREB/VEGFA通路改善卒中后恢复，仅涉及分子对接筛选活性成分，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and cognitive impairment. Yindan Xinnaotong Soft Capsule (YD), a traditional Chinese patent medicine, is clinically utilized for cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, yet its potential roles in post-stroke recovery remains unclear. PURPOSE: To elucidate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of YD on ischemic post-stroke recovery. METHODS: Middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) models were utilized to investigate the effects of YD on post-stroke recovery. Cerebral atrophy (TTC staining), histopathology (H&E, Nissl, and Golgi staining), synaptic ultrastructure (transmission electron microscopy, TEM), and behavioral tests were assessed. RNA-seq and network pharmacology analysis were utilized to reveal the underlying mechanisms, and verified in brain tissues, 2D monolayer cell, and 3D neurovascular unit (NVU) spheroids. Molecular docking was performed to screen the potential active ingredients and verified by immunofluorescence and cellular thermal shift assay. RESULTS: YD significantly alleviated post-stroke brain atrophy volume, neurological deficit score, cognitive/motor deficit, and pathological structure and hippocampal synaptic ultrastructure damage. A total of 535 differentially expressed genes analysis revealed that CREB signaling with the key targets of CREB, BDNF, and VEGFA was the central mechanism. The synaptic plasticity marker of synaptophysin and angiogenesis marker of CD31 were upregulated in brain tissues and 3D NVU spheroids mediated by CREB/BDNF and CREB/VEGFA pathway, respectively. Co-treatment with the CREB inhibitor 666-15 attenuated YD's effects on CREB phosphorylation. Salvianolic acid B (from Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge) and Kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside (from Ginkgo biloba leaf) were identified and validated as primary active ingredients with high CREB affinity. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrated that YD promoted post-ischemic stroke recovery by promoting CREB/BDNF-mediated synaptic plasticity and CREB/VEGFA-mediated angiogenesis, highlighting its therapeutic potential for treating long-term cerebral ischemia injury.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血性卒中（ischemic stroke）是导致残疾和认知障碍的主要原因之一。银丹心脑通软胶囊（YD）作为一种传统中成药，临床上用于心脑血管疾病，但其在卒中后恢复中的潜在作用尚不明确。目的：阐明YD对缺血性卒中后恢复的保护作用及其潜在机制。方法：采用大脑中动脉闭塞/再灌注（MCAO/R）和氧糖剥夺/再灌注（OGD/R）模型，研究YD对卒中后恢复的影响。评估脑萎缩（TTC染色）、组织病理学（H&E、Nissl和Golgi染色）、突触超微结构（透射电子显微镜，TEM）及行为学测试。利用RNA测序（RNA-seq）和网络药理学分析揭示潜在机制，并在脑组织、二维单层细胞和三维神经血管单元（NVU）球体中进行验证。通过分子对接筛选潜在活性成分，并采用免疫荧光和细胞热位移分析进行验证。结果：YD显著减轻了卒中后脑萎缩体积、神经功能缺损评分、认知/运动障碍以及病理结构和海马突触超微结构损伤。共535个差异表达基因分析显示，以CREB、BDNF和VEGFA为关键靶点的CREB信号通路是核心机制。突触可塑性标志物突触素和血管生成标志物CD31在脑组织和三维NVU球体中分别通过CREB/BDNF和CREB/VEGFA通路上调。与CREB抑制剂666-15共处理减弱了YD对CREB磷酸化的影响。丹酚酸B（来源于丹参，Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge）和山柰酚-3-O-芸香糖苷（来源于银杏叶，Ginkgo biloba leaf）被鉴定并验证为具有高CREB亲和力的主要活性成分。结论：本研究表明，YD通过促进CREB/BDNF介导的突触可塑性和CREB/VEGFA介导的血管生成，促进缺血性卒中后恢复，凸显了其治疗长期脑缺血损伤的潜力。
